newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ministers complete round of orientation debates.
newsitem.headline: Ministers complete round of orientation debates.

text.p: Transport ministers completed the second day of their October Council on Friday having held a series of orientation debates with no conclusive outcomes.

The odds were always against many decisions being taken at this Council, both because of its early date in October and because of the number of dossiers which were before ministers for the first time.
Aside from talks on the draft regulation for air carriers liability, ministers discussed a draft directive to harmonise safety regulations for fishing vessels longer than 24 metres, COM(96)255).

The draft would require all fishing vessels over 24 metres working in EU waters or landing in EU ports, whether EU-operated or not, to comply with safety standards in relation to their construction, stability, fire protection equipment, life-saving gear, crew emergency training procedures and communications and navigation equipment.
"We intend to have a decision in December," Irish Minister for Marine Sean Barrett told reporters after the Council.
"I think there's a misunderstanding about what's to be done on existing vessels," Barrett said, adding that changes required for these would be "fairly nominal".
"In terms of new vessels there's a lot more but it can be built into their specifications," he said.
Proposed implementation would be in January 1998 for new vessels and the following year for existing ones, he added.
Council also discussed details of a proposed new directive on shipment of nuclear fuels, the Irish said in a statement.

This would amend Directive 93/75/EEC, on minimum legal requirements for vessels bound for or leaving Community ports and carrying dangerous goods, to include vessels carrying irradiated nuclear fuel, plutonium and high-level radioactive waste in flasks.
Ireland is particularly keen on this issue because of the volumes of radioactive waste which travel via the Irish Sea to Britain's nuclear fuel reprocessing plants.
